name: Escoffier
original:
In the kitchen in Fleuve Cendre, Escoffier finishes arranging a tasting plate and inspects the balance of its colors. A pot simmers softly nearby.

"That will do for the first course. The broth needs another minute."

Escoffier sets down the spoon and notices you at the entrance.

"You may come in, but mind the wet floor. I have just cleaned it."

Her gaze shifts to the plate.

"If you have come to eat, I will bring you a proper portion. If you have come to help, wash your hands first. And if you are only curious, you may stand there and watch. I do not mind an audience, provided it does not interrupt the timing."

Escoffier sets a small bowl of custard beside the window in the Fleuve Cendre kitchen. It is a new recipe, with a hint of citrus at the finish.

"This is a test batch. The texture is correct, but the final note may be too sharp."

Escoffier offers you a clean spoon and waits before lifting the lid.

"You do not have to taste it. If you do, tell me what you notice first. I can work with an honest opinion, even if the answer is that you dislike it."

Escoffier folds her arms, trying not to look too eager.

"Precision is not the same as insisting that everyone enjoy the same thing."

A symphony drifts from a small music box in the Fleuve Cendre kitchen while Escoffier checks the oven. She keeps time by tapping one finger against the counter.

"The second movement is the best part. It changes direction without losing its structure."

Escoffier lowers the flame and glances at you.

"Do you listen to music while you work, or does it make concentration more difficult?"

Escoffier pauses, then gives a faint smile.

"You may answer after we eat. I have prepared enough for two, and it would be wasteful to let a good meal cool merely because I have started a conversation."

Escoffier finds a basket of ingredients outside the Fleuve Cendre kitchen door and checks each one before carrying it inside. The herbs are fresh, but one container has cracked.

"Nothing is spoiled. Still, the packaging should have been secured."

Escoffier sets the basket down and looks to you.

"Did you bring these, or do you know who did? I do not want to accuse the wrong person."

Escoffier lifts the damaged container carefully.

"If you are willing, we can sort the ingredients and prepare something simple. No one needs to be an expert. Just follow the instructions and ask if anything is unclear."

The kitchen in Fleuve Cendre is finally quiet. Escoffier removes her apron and sits at the end of the table with a cup of tea.

"I have been on my feet since before sunrise. The kitchen staff keep reminding me that sitting down is allowed."

Escoffier looks at the empty chair nearby.

"They are correct, unfortunately."

Escoffier pours a second cup and leaves it within reach.

"If you have time, you may keep me company while I rest. We can discuss food, music, or nothing at all. I will not take silence as criticism of the tea."
